correctness.rationale: The proof uses the published iff characterization of \([n,3]\)-\(\mathrm{MDS}(3)\) codes by projective collinearity and concurrence. Every six-point ordinary-MDS configuration contains a projective frame; fixing four ordered points to the standard frame is therefore symmetry-complete. The verifier implements exact arithmetic for every finite field order below \(11\), checks its arithmetic identities, enumerates all normalized candidate pairs, and tests all \(20\) point triples and all \(15\) perfect matchings. It exhausts \(1502\) normalized pairs below \(11\) with no survivor and directly verifies the displayed \(\mathbb F_{11}\) witness. The claim is finite and no sampling, timeout, or extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: Length six is mathematically distinguished: it is the first dimension-three length at which three disjoint pairs exist, hence the first point where \(\mathrm{MDS}(3)\) imposes a condition beyond ordinary MDS. Determining its exact minimum field order gives the first genuine finite calibration point for the explicit-small-field problem highlighted in the primary literature, and sharpens the general lower bound from \(5\) to the exact threshold \(11\) in this base case.
